correctness.rationale: Complete analytic argument: support additivity yields exact interval-range formula, and Gaussian radius-direction independence yields finite mean integral. A joint upper/lower Gaussian extremal point-process limit gives independent spatial PPP limits. Gaussian-hazard bounds on scaled maxima, with negligible sub-sqrt(n) window lengths, establish Lp uniform short-window control and continuity/truncation for macroscopic windows. Chi inverse-radius moments make the direction normalization vanish in L2. Gumbel interval-max distributions give the mean constant gamma-3/2 and positive finite variance; a rare-high-mark event gives an exponential tail lower bound, excluding Gaussianity. The actual embedded finite checker passes. Risks: stochastic process mapping relies on standard point-process convergence, proved via Laplace-functional rare-event reasoning; numerical tests cannot prove infinite limits.

value.rationale: A complete non-Gaussian random-width limit for the canonical path associahedron, not a routine restatement of an expected support value. Spatial overlap among all consecutive intervals retains a Poisson location functional distinct from an individual Gumbel maximum. The second-order mean constant, exact finite mean and positive limiting variance quantify an intrinsic geometric invariant; the all-interval structure is motivated by the path building set, not an arbitrary parameter slice. Risks: only the unweighted intrinsic realization and one-dimensional projections are covered; no explicit closed form for the limiting variance is claimed.
